exposure: Gestational weight gain (classified as too low, recommended, or too high according to IOM guidelines)
Maternal pre-pregnancy weight status (underweight, normal-weight, overweight, obese, morbidly obese)
outcome: Fetal growth (birth weight, birth length, head circumference)
Neonatal vital parameters (APGAR scores, umbilical cord pH values)
cohort: The study analyzed data from 11,755 singleton births that occurred between 2010 and 2020 at the Public Clinic Donaustadt in Vienna, Austria.
finding: Excessive gestational weight gain was associated with enhanced fetal growth and an increased risk of macrosomia and emergency cesarean sections, with these associations varying significantly across different maternal pre-pregnancy weight categories, indicating the IOM guidelines may need reconsideration for certain groups.
mod_finding: A too-high gestational weight gain was significantly associated with an increased risk of emergency cesarean sections among underweight, normal-weight, and overweight women, while among obese mothers, a too-low gestational weight gain significantly reduced this risk.
